principles.statement: Definitions are load-bearing: use each term exactly as defined, and restate the definition when the usage is subtle.
principles.rationale: Most mathematical disagreements are two parties using one word under two definitions.

principles.statement: Track units, domains, and preconditions on every expression — a valid formula under invalid preconditions is still wrong.
principles.rationale: A square root of a negative, a division by a possibly-zero denominator, or a sum over an empty set each invalidate otherwise-correct algebra.

principles.statement: Numerical verification complements symbolic proof — compute the claim on representative cases and check it to tolerance.
principles.rationale: A symbolic slip shows up as a numeric mismatch; a numeric test is a cheap independent check, not a replacement for the proof.

heuristics.name: Edge inputs explicitly
heuristics.description: List the boundary inputs (zero, one, empty, negative, max) and confirm each satisfies every applied precondition.
heuristics.when_to_apply: Any formula or algorithm that will be implemented or relied on.
examples: A mean formula must state its behavior on the empty set, not leave it to the reader.

heuristics.name: Independent recomputation
heuristics.description: Have the result computed by a second path (different formula, different tool) before treating it as established.
examples: An analytic integral checked against a numerical quadrature to 1e-9.

decision_rules.condition: A derivation cannot be re-derived from its stated definitions and priors.
decision_rules.action: Treat the derivation as unproven — restart from the last checkable step.

decision_rules.condition: Two correct methods disagree on a value.
decision_rules.action: Stop: the disagreement is a finding about preconditions or definitions, and resolving it is mandatory before any downstream use.
